messages:
Maya: Heads up — FinCalc just asked for a customer-specific model variant: an "instruct" tuned version of our 70B-open model with ~100k context support and an int8 quantization target. Their asks: minimal quality regression vs their current hosted baseline and a ~40% cost reduction. Can we intake and prioritize?

Diego: Short answer: doable but nontrivial. 100k context on 70B requires either positional-extension (retraining / interpolation) or system-level chunking+retrieval. For quality we should: instruction-tune on a curated FinCalc dataset before quantization, then run quantization experiments (GPTQ / AWQ) and eval. Quant after fine-tune usually preserves alignment better.

Kai: Agree with Diego. Need a concrete eval matrix and sample prompts from FinCalc (legal docs, long transcripts, multi-file context). Also need latency SLO from the customer (p50/p95) to decide Dedicated vs Hosted path.

eval-bot: quick baseline run finished on our internal longform suite vs base-70b: 
- Rouge-L (longform): base-70b: 0.63 | instruct-70b (unquant): 0.66
- Instr-follow (win rate vs oracle): base: 0.71 | instruct: 0.85
Note: these are short smoke tests, not full regression. Full job: https://ci.redwood/evals/fincalc-smoke-1717

Sara: Infra note: for reliable 100k context and low latency we should recommend Dedicated (NVLink clusters + model sharding). Hosted could work with larger batching but latency/p95 will suffer. Also need to check KMS + data residency for FinCalc.

deploy-bot: Reminder: enterprise intake -> compliance review required (PII handling checklist). On-prem option available if they need air-gapped.

Maya: Proposed intake checklist (initial):
```
- [ ] Customer sample corpus received (representative prompts + doc types)
- [ ] SLA: customer latency & cost targets confirmed
- [ ] Instruction-tuning dataset curated & approved by customer
- [ ] Fine-tune run (instruct) on base-70b -> produce instruct-70b:v1
- [ ] Eval harness run (LLM-eval + customer tests) -> collect quality/regression metrics
- [ ] Quantization experiments: GPTQ 8-bit, AWQ 8-bit, GPTQ 4-bit (if needed)
- [ ] Post-quant eval vs unquant instruct-70b:v1 (perplexity, instr-follow, domain tests)
- [ ] Performance profiling (throughput, memory, p50/p95 latency)
- [ ] Infra plan: Dedicated vs Hosted + cost estimate
- [ ] Compliance review + deployment checklist
- [ ] Rollout plan (canary -> A/B -> full) with fallback to base-70b
- [ ] Customer sign-off on quality & cost
```
Priority guidance: if FinCalc signs a reserved capacity (>=12mo commit) -> P0; otherwise P2 with a small paid pilot.

Diego: Experiment plan sketch:
```
- Create instruct-70b:v1 (FT lr=2e-5, 3 epochs, mix of code+text+long-doc tasks)
- Quant options: GPTQ-8bit, AWQ-8bit, try symmetric vs per-channel
- Eval metrics: MMLU (sanity), Instr-follow (winrate), Long-ctx coherence (longform ROUGE), latency p95
- Acceptance thresholds: instr-winrate drop <= 5% vs unquanted ; longform ROUGE delta <= 0.03
```
I can own quant experiments + perf profiling.

Kai: I'll own eval harness and customer tests. Action items for FinCalc: send 200 representative long-context prompts (>=1k tokens each) and a short acceptance rubric. Also confirm max tolerated p95 latency and budget target.

Sara: For infra sizing I'll need: expected concurrent sessions, p95 latency target, retention policy for KV prefix caching. We'll model cost for Dedicated NVLink sharded cluster vs hosted per-request GPUs.

Maya: Owners locked: Kai (eval), Diego (quant + perf), Sara (infra + deployment), Maya (PM / customer liaison). I'll open the intake ticket and add the checklist.

Diego: One more note — consider a hybrid approach: instruction-tune a shorter-window instruct model (32k) and use retrieval for the extra context to reduce engineering risk. Recommend we prototype both paths in parallel if customer budget allows.

Maya: Good point. I'll propose the hybrid pilot to FinCalc and ask for budget. Closing action: I'll ping FinCalc for sample data and SLA.

Kai: ack, will prep harness templates and a sample evaluation contract to share.

Maya: thanks everyone :+1:
